releases.title: Player fixes: Crown checks, duel recovery and Achievements
releases.summary: Clearer Crown eligibility and retry states, finite-spare duel recovery, reachable Achievements and corrected world effects and interactions.
evidence: Compared the previous production game with the exact compiled release candidate.
Focused offline browser verification across desktop, phone landscape and phone portrait, with external writes blocked.
Public wiki entries and standard model assets reviewed against the same candidate.

sections.title: Crown Herald and linked fighter loading
items: Fighter-association and directory loading now distinguish a verified missing record from a failed request. A temporary service failure no longer tells an existing player to register or link again. Optional statistics failures do not discard a verified fighter association. Responses for an old signed-in account cannot replace the current account’s result.

The Crown Herald shows loading, recoverable errors and a Retry fighter and crown check control. Challenge controls stay unavailable until the relevant check completes. Leaving the panel while a request is pending does not reopen it over unrelated navigation.

A read-only check uses the signed-in account and separates association, directory, eligible roster, competition division, current holder and confirmed Royal writ progression. A writ present only on the device is explained as awaiting cloud confirmation. Existing requirements remain in force; a successful check does not itself grant a Crown.
The existing Crown fight, verdict retry and title-transfer rules remain in use. No player associations or eligibility records were changed to make a test pass.

Installed-browser asset caching now excludes personal Crown eligibility. Checks always use the network; offline checks show a reconnect-and-retry error instead of a cached account result. The updated game cache identity also refreshes the application package.

sections.title: Ordinary duel equipment recovery
items: An ordinary duel no longer remains stuck after its finite corner replacements are exhausted. When no usable category-legal reserve remains, and no legal sidearm is being drawn, the marshal pauses the fight clock for an equipment check. Existing sidearm drawing completes before this recovery path.

An intact, category-legal original weapon can be returned without creating a new spare. The human competitor uses Collect my weapon. An AI competitor resumes after three simulation seconds. The real animation loop now advances this equipment-check phase, including background bouts. Recorded points and remaining reserve stock are preserved.

When no intact legal original weapon is available, the equipment allowance lasts 60 seconds. If legal equipment is still unavailable at expiry, the duel ends by technical decision. The player can withdraw earlier. Results and share text identify the technical decision and recorded points rather than implying that extra hit points were scored.

The corner still starts with two replacements per side. Replacements respect the existing duel category. This release does not change ordinary best-of-three round scoring, Pro fights, training or Crown NPC combat. Background festival duels recover without opening a panel over town menus.

The pause is not immunity: the existing penalties for striking an unarmed competitor remain, including foul points and warning, yellow and red card consequences. Recovery cannot replenish reserve stock or erase cards.

Previously, exhaustion could leave a bout unresolved; there was no verified finite recovery duration to compare. The new 60-second allowance and three-simulation-second AI return are behavior definitions, not measured performance improvements or a percentage reduction in match time.

sections.title: Achievements and narrow-screen navigation
items: The Fighter screen now labels its entry Progress / Achievements. Achievements has an explicit selectable tab. Narrow screens wrap the controls so the entry remains reachable in portrait and landscape, including enlarged text.

The selected Fighter page and scroll position survive navigation away and reopening. Existing earned achievements remain in the career save; the interface change does not grant achievements or alter their requirements.

metrics.name: Fighter top-tab minimum height on screens up to 900 CSS pixels wide
metrics.context: CSS minimum target height; actual rendered height may be larger. The absolute increase is 6 CSS pixels; this is not a measured input-accuracy improvement.

sections.title: World effects and interaction consistency
items: The furnace opening glow now follows the furnace model’s local transform. Leaving and re-entering town retains one live opening effect. Crafting recipes, material costs and furnace collision are unchanged.

Interaction prompts now agree with active, visible objects and their reachable approach. Detached or inactive visuals do not retain usable prompts. Moved gathering visuals retain their original resource identity and cooldown. Further details of undisclosed content are intentionally omitted.

sections.title: Wiki coverage and release compatibility
items: The wiki adds public guides for duel equipment recovery, Crown Herald checks and finding Achievements. Existing public articles and historical patch-note links remain available. Standard armoury geometry and static previews are refreshed against this exact game build.
This release uses the existing live game and /wiki/ routes. Existing player saves, ordinary duel formats and the shared Crown verification protocol are preserved. It introduces no save migration.
No measured frame-rate, latency or memory improvement is claimed. The changes address recovery behavior, information clarity, navigation and visual alignment.
Player reports: Keston Piche. Development: Garrett Robson, with AI assistance.

metrics.name: Reviewed public wiki entries
metrics.context: Three verified public system guides added; no hidden-content entries.

knownIssues: A genuine eligible linked-account Crown success has not been verified online because the automated testing account has no eligible fighter association. Offline linked-account, service-error and verdict scenarios are tested; this does not establish the state of any individual player’s private record.
Physical Android, controller hardware and separate-device/WAN play have not been verified for this release. Phone browser automation does not substitute for those tests.
validation: 51 focused offline browser cases passed across desktop, phone landscape and phone portrait, including real animation-loop recovery, finite stock, legal sidearms, foul penalties, technical decisions, full-save retry, Achievements persistence, furnace rendering and interaction lifecycle.

41 source, authentication, worker and isolated database tests passed, including profile-error distinctions, eligibility ownership, read-only preflight behavior, replay determinism and existing Crown reservation/claim rules.

Existing production authentication-return, menu, mount-control, Crown replay/verdict, armour-repair and Gauntlet regressions passed. Existing production duel formats and squire repair behavior are preserved.

Read-only online testing with the persistent automated account passed desktop, phone landscape and phone portrait: account restore/reload, unlinked Crown status and retry, Achievements, furnace and re-entry. No Crown challenge was started and the account save was unchanged.

Public catalogue, numerical-note calculations, all 232 articles, 19 standard model/display assets, static previews, armoury comparison/dressing room, responsive search/navigation, permanent notes links and service-worker bypass checks passed locally.

releases.title: The armoury: live models, dressing room and gear comparisons
releases.summary: Explore the game's standard equipment in 3D, try a full kit on an armoured fighter, and compare equipment stats side by side.
evidence: Based on the exact game page and renderer served by production commit 8435291da751e28205983fa2e7df44ebbbd98d94, build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73.

Model geometry and materials were serialized from the live game's standard equipment and anonymous display-fighter constructors. Every exported equipment ID already belongs to the reviewed public catalogue.
The model manifest records game-source, renderer, geometry and preview-image SHA-256 hashes. Models contain self-contained textures and no executable game bundle, account exports or save data.
The interface follows patterns researched in Wowhead's model-viewer tutorial and transmog tools: https://www.wowhead.com/news/wowhead-modelviewer-tutorial-235544 and https://www.wowhead.com/transmog.

sections.title: A visual equipment database
items: A new Armoury page shows the seven standard weapons, eight helmets and two shields with rendered images of their actual game geometry. Each card links to its existing item article and offers Try on and Compare actions.

Search by equipment name or description, filter by equipment type or weapon hand count, and sort alphabetically, by ascending mass, or by descending weapon reach. Empty searches explain how to broaden the filters.
The wiki overview, desktop sidebar, header and mobile browse drawer now link to the armoury and dressing room. Existing quest, material, crafting, place and skill articles remain available.

metrics.name: Standard equipment models available for inspection
metrics.context: New wiki model previews; the equipment already existed in the game.

sections.title: Interactive character and equipment viewers
items: Equipment articles now offer Explore in 3D. Rotate with a pointer, keyboard arrows or the rotation buttons; zoom with the slider, plus/minus keys or a two-finger pinch. Reset restores the starting camera. Auto rotate is optional and pauses rendering while the page is hidden or the viewer is outside the viewport.

The dressing room assembles standard weapons, helmets and shields on either the standard or fitted anonymous armoured harness. Geometry, materials and Reavers colours come from the game. Mannequins use a fixed 1.8 m display body; camera, pedestal, lighting and inspection pose are wiki presentation.
Changing to a two-handed weapon removes and disables the shield. Changing back to a one-handed weapon makes the shield selector available again; a shield is optional.

Fighter-archetype articles also show an armoured display fighter and link to the dressing room. These are illustrative mannequins, not reconstructions of a specific player or a promise that an archetype fixes your personal appearance.

metrics.name: Anonymous harness shapes in the dressing room
metrics.context: Standard and fitted display mannequins; no player character is imported.

sections.title: Compare, save and share
items: Select up to three pieces of the same equipment type in the armoury. Mixed types are rejected with an explanation, and the selection can be cleared.

The comparison shows actual source stats and absolute differences from the first selected piece. Weapons compare mass, reach, hand count and class; helmets compare mass, protection, field of view, breathing and sound muffling; shields compare mass and block value. Larger values are not universally better, and these source values do not measure match outcomes.
Each comparison and dressing-room combination has its own shareable URL. Copy-link controls use the clipboard when available and provide a selectable link when clipboard access is unavailable.
Save up to five looks in this browser and reopen or remove them later. Saved looks do not sync to a game account and never equip, purchase or change anything in the game.
The displayed equipment mass subtotal includes only the selected weapon, helmet and optional shield. It excludes body armour and all other carried kit; it is not the fighter's total kit mass.

metrics.name: Saved dressing-room looks per browser
metrics.context: Maximum locally stored looks; clearing browser storage removes them.

sections.title: Mobile, accessibility and loading behavior
items: The armoury uses responsive cards, labelled filters and touch-sized controls. Dressing-room controls stack under the model on phones; wide comparison tables remain horizontally scrollable.
The Three.js renderer loads only after a visitor requests a 3D preview. Ordinary wiki browsing uses static model images and does not create a WebGL context.

If the renderer or a model cannot be loaded, the static preview and equipment facts remain accessible. Leaving a page disposes its model geometry, textures and renderer. Reduced-motion preferences disable card movement; model auto-rotation requires an explicit click.
The viewer uses the game's existing Three.js r149 with its MIT license. Quaternius CC0 source geometry credits are retained with the model assets.

sections.title: Release scope and maintenance
items: This is a wiki-only release inside the existing live game's /wiki/ folder. The game home screen, small Wiki link, engine code, gameplay values, progression and saves are unchanged.
The existing 229-entry public catalogue and permanent release archive are retained. Only reviewed standard equipment and the anonymous display mannequins join the public asset allowlist.

Future release maintenance now includes live-model extraction, static-preview generation and manifest checks against the exact candidate game page. Unknown equipment remains subject to individual public-content review.
Published silently under the owner's continuing request. No Discord announcement is sent.

knownIssues: WebGL support and performance depend on the browser and device. Static previews are always available; physical-device pinch and performance measurements have not been performed.
Personal character import, account synchronization, cosmetic variants, wear/damage states and gameplay animations are not part of this inspection viewer.
validation: All 19 model assets parsed and rendered to their static previews, including every standard equipment piece and both harness shapes.
Gallery searches, filters, sorting, comparison selection and arithmetic, kit deep links, two-hand/shield behavior and saved-look persistence tested at desktop and 390/320 px phone widths.
3D triangle rendering, rotation, keyboard zoom/reset, model switching, renderer disposal and graphics-load failure fallback tested in browser automation.
Existing catalogue, quest-link, release arithmetic, search, mobile navigation and public article checks retained.

releases.title: Restore the original main-menu layout
releases.summary: The extra Wiki row is removed. A small Wiki link joins Settings and Credits without moving the original menu.
evidence: Compared with production commit 66a6b3181651b5a578c620fb4f4003e74a90a36e and the original menu markup.
The engine page, existing menu stylesheet, gameplay assets and save format are unchanged.

sections.title: Correct the menu layout
items: The previous separate Wiki row increased the menu height and shifted the centred title layout. This corrects the placement introduced in game-menu-wiki and retained in game-menu-wiki-compact.
Wiki is now a small text link in the existing Settings and Credits row. It does not create an additional menu row or use the primary button style.
The existing title, division controls, Time to Fight, Settings and Credits retain their original positions and sizes. The external-browser request and HTTPS fallback are preserved.
This changes only the menu-link UI asset and its cache revision. Reload or restart an already running game to receive it. No combat or progression values change.
Deployed silently at the owner's request. No Discord announcement.

knownIssues: The operating system and browser still control external-app handoff; physical Android/iOS handoff has not been tested.
validation: Original home element positions and sizes compared before and after link insertion at desktop, landscape-phone and two portrait-phone sizes.
Separate-window opening, null opener and duplicate prevention checked in browser automation.

releases.title: A compact Wiki button
releases.summary: The Wiki link beneath Time to Fight is now a small, centred secondary button.
evidence: Compared with production commit 72fece0a2aedd888733f455b8ad78ebf28003046.
Only the existing menu UI asset, its cache revision and this permanent release record change.

sections.title: Smaller menu link
items: The Wiki link no longer uses the large primary-button style. It fits its label in a centred button, with 14 px text, 16 px horizontal padding, and a width between 96 and 140 px.
The minimum touch-target height remains 44 px. Keyboard focus, external-browser intent and HTTPS fallback keep their existing behavior.
This UI-asset revision leaves gameplay values, the engine build and saves unchanged. Reload or restart an already running game to receive the revised cached menu asset.
Published silently at the owner's request; no Discord announcement.

knownIssues: Final app-to-browser handoff remains controlled by the device. It has not been tested on physical Android or iOS hardware.
validation: Button placement, compact width and 44 px target checked on desktop and portrait/landscape phones.
External link behavior, Android intent/fallback and duplicate protection checked with browser automation.

releases.title: Open the wiki from the main menu
releases.summary: A Wiki button is available directly below Time to Fight, with an external-browser request that keeps the game page open.
evidence: Based on production commit b5be3892f62909f7a8e7dc0c7a0b2b0a3dc15f29 and game build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73.
The existing menu UI asset adds the link; the game engine page and save format are preserved. The service-worker asset-cache revision changes so reloaded installed games receive the new menu asset.
Android intent syntax follows https://developer.chrome.com/docs/android/intents. Installed-web-app behavior remains controlled by the device and browser.

sections.title: A wiki button on the game menu
items: A clearly labelled Wiki button appears directly below Time to Fight. It uses the existing menu styling, supports keyboard and controller focus, and links to the full player wiki on the live server.
The link opens a new browsing context with opener access disabled, so it does not replace the current game page.

The existing game UI script supplies the button and guards against duplicate insertion. Cached UI assets receive a new service-worker cache revision; an already running game may need a reload or restart to show the button.

sections.title: Opening outside the installed game
items: On Android in standalone, fullscreen or minimal-UI display mode, the button requests Chrome through an Android browser intent. An HTTPS fallback is included if the intent cannot be handled.
Other environments use a standard HTTPS link with target=_blank and rel=external, noopener and noreferrer. This requests a separate browser window or tab and keeps the game page open.

A website cannot universally force a particular external browser or override every installed-app, operating-system or embedded-browser policy. Device handoff is therefore best effort, rather than a promise that every platform will leave its app container.

sections.title: Scope and validation
items: This release adds menu navigation. It changes no combat values, progression, costs, XP, rewards, player saves or public game-content entries.
The embedded engine build remains steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73; this is a separate UI-asset/cache revision.
The owner requested a silent update. No Discord announcement is sent for this release.

knownIssues: Actual Android/iOS app-to-browser handoff has not been tested on a physical device. Native new-window behavior and generated Android intent/fallback paths are covered by browser automation.
If Chrome is unavailable or the host blocks external launches, the operating system/browser decides how to handle the HTTPS fallback.
validation: Main-menu link placement and usable target size checked at desktop, landscape-phone and portrait-phone dimensions.
Native new-window opening, null opener and preservation of the original game page checked in browser automation.
Standalone/fullscreen Android intent construction, HTTPS fallback, duplicate protection and the iOS standalone link path checked with simulated environments.

releases.title: A field guide that feels at home on your phone
releases.summary: A refreshed interface with easier phone navigation, typo-tolerant search, saved entries, two reading themes and better tools for long articles.
evidence: Compared with production commit 48da0e78d013dcbc2eba8d783102bd79786acb7d, gameplay build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73.
Fuse.js 7.5.0 and a 29-icon Lucide Static 1.57.0 subset are pinned, served locally, and accompanied by their license files and vendor hashes.
Declared typography values compared with the previous production wiki CSS. Percentages describe CSS font-size changes, not gameplay or measured player outcomes.

sections.title: Made for phone navigation
items: A compact sticky header and a dedicated navigation drawer replace the horizontal category strip on narrow screens. The drawer exposes every database category and the link back to the game.
A bottom navigation bar keeps Explore, Search, Updates and Saved within reach. Controls account for the phone's bottom safe area, and the page reserves room beneath the content.
Cards, quick facts, article layouts and dialogs adjust to narrow phones, tablets and desktop windows. Wide numerical patch-note tables remain scrollable, with an explanatory hint and keyboard focus.

sections.title: Find an entry even when the spelling is imperfect
items: Fuse.js adds typo-tolerant matching to the wiki search. Exact matches are retained, while additional close matches help with misspelled names and multi-word queries.

A site-wide search dialog is available from any article, using the header button, the phone's Search tab, or Ctrl+K / Command+K. The slash shortcut focuses the current page's search when available and opens site search elsewhere.

Arrow keys move through site-search suggestions, Enter opens a focused entry, and Escape dismisses the dialog. Search, icons and their supporting library files are served by the game server; no external search service receives queries.

sections.title: Keep your own useful pages
items: Every database article has a Save entry control. Saved entries have their own page, persist across reloads on the same browser and can be removed individually or cleared.

The home page can show recently opened articles so a player can return to a quest, ingredient or location. Recent and saved pages are stored locally in this browser; they do not sync with a game account or another device.
Copy page link shares an entry or the canonical full-release URL. If clipboard access is unavailable, the interface opens a selectable link for manual copying.

sections.title: Reading, themes and long-page tools
items: The visual refresh uses a forest-and-brass dark palette, a parchment light palette, consistent Lucide icons, clearer cards, rounded surfaces and more consistent spacing.
The theme switch stores the reader's choice in this browser. Larger article and result text improves the default reading scale; browser zoom remains available.
Long articles and release notes gain an On this page section list. The list can be collapsed on phones, and its buttons move keyboard focus to the chosen heading.

A reading progress line and a back-to-top control help with longer pages. Reduced-motion preferences disable animated transitions and smooth scrolling. Native dialogs provide focus containment and Escape handling.

metrics.name: Quest chapter paragraph and objective font size
metrics.context: Default declared chapter copy and objective size in the wiki; this is a typography change, not a gameplay change.

metrics.name: Search result title font size
metrics.context: Default declared title size in the standard results list.

metrics.name: Search result description font size
metrics.context: Default declared summary size in standard page search results; compact dialog suggestions may use a smaller summary.

sections.title: Compatibility, scope and verification
items: This release changes the wiki interface. The game page, game build, saves, combat, costs, XP, rewards and existing release records are preserved.
The public catalogue remains subject to its existing review policy. Secrets, discovery clues, hidden content and private player data are not added by these interface features.

Interactive preferences rely on browser storage. If storage is unavailable, the current page still works but saved entries and preferences cannot be retained. Saved pages are specific to the current browser and origin.
Search dialogs use the browser's native dialog support. Font fallbacks remain available if the optional web fonts cannot load. No measured speed or frame-rate gain is claimed.

knownIssues: Saved entries, recent pages and theme preferences do not sync across browsers or devices.
The existing guide coverage gaps remain: this interface update does not add unverified gameplay content.
validation: Responsive interface checks at 320, 390, 768 and 1440 CSS pixels, including dark and light themes and horizontal-overflow checks.
Checks cover typo-tolerant search, search keyboard navigation, drawer dismissal, saved-entry persistence/removal, theme persistence, article jump links, Escape dismissal and reduced-motion behavior.
Existing catalogue, quest-link, recipe, release arithmetic, archive, exported-subfolder and service-worker checks remain part of the release gate.

releases.title: A live reference and permanent full patch notes
releases.summary: The player reference is checked against the current game, with permanent detailed release pages and clearer release timestamps.
evidence: Verified production gameplay build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73 at commit 0e44bd249c19314bb661eb7271bc02048db5e2df before this wiki-only update.
Live-source refresh verified 229 public entries, no changed entries and no new pending entries. Gameplay files are preserved byte-for-byte.

sections.title: The current player reference
items: The wiki was refreshed from the actual live game. Its 229 reviewed public entries and their player-facing values were unchanged in this refresh.

Quest chapters, prerequisites, objectives, ordinary rewards, people and places, gathering requirements, recipes, equipment and combat perks remain searchable and linked. No new gameplay system is claimed by this release.

sections.title: Detailed release records
items: The patch-note archive keeps permanent links for individual releases, including this page. Existing release entries remain intact. Factual corrections will be published as new records identifying the earlier claim.
Release facts now display the release time with the date and timezone. Search and direct release links continue to work from the wiki subfolder.

Full notes accompany future game updates and explain affected modes, conditions, mechanics, fixes, interactions, edge cases, compatibility and known issues. The short Discord announcement points to the complete public record.

sections.title: Understanding numerical changes
items: Future numerical changes use verified old and new values, explicit units, the absolute difference and the relative percentage change. Percentage-valued statistics also show percentage-point differences.

A zero baseline has no defined relative percentage change. Unknown old values are identified as unknown rather than guessed. Source constants and calculated percentages do not establish measured performance or win-rate improvements.

This release changes the wiki and release workflow. It does not change gameplay balance, costs, XP, ordinary rewards, cooldowns, probabilities, save formats or controls; there are no numerical gameplay deltas to report.

sections.title: Compatibility and verification
items: The current gameplay build is retained, including the latest fixes already present in production. No player-save migration is required for this wiki update.
The wiki and full notes remain under the live game domain. Wiki requests use the existing network-only behavior rather than the game offline cache.
Content, link, numeric-note and desktop/phone browser checks cover the reference and full-note pages. No measured frame-rate or loading-speed improvement is claimed.

knownIssues: Coverage is still incomplete for public cosmetics, housing, full mode walkthroughs, detailed controls and advanced squire care. The coverage page continues to identify these gaps.
Physical Android and real-account multi-device gameplay acceptance are outside this wiki-only verification.
validation: Live-source extraction: matching production build, 229 reviewed entries, no pending additions and no catalogue changes.
Release archive preserves the earlier wiki-launch record and its permanent URL.

releases.title: The Steel & Tape player wiki is here
releases.summary: A searchable player reference and a permanent home for detailed patch notes, hosted alongside the live game.
evidence: Verified current production game build steel-tape-auth-ad27047a6f73, Git commit 5a888e39016e6034cb0b0d7ca10cb4110044ce14. The wiki release preserves that gameplay build.
229-entry public catalogue validated with 88 quest chapters; desktop and phone browser checks passed

sections.title: The player database
items: 22 questlines contain 88 chapters, with prerequisites, objectives, gold and XP rewards, dialogue choices and follow-up quests.
10 public regions and 10 arenas link to 67 people and services. Region pages include world coordinates, access requirements and regional gathering information.
The first catalogue includes 17 standard equipment pieces, 19 materials, 6 trades, 45 combat perks, 22 core crafting recipes, 4 repeatable contracts and 5 fighter archetypes.
Search supports names, objectives, ingredients, places and other entry details. Articles link to related quests, NPCs, materials and prerequisites.

sections.title: A home for full patch notes
items: Detailed release pages live at /wiki/patch-notes/ and have permanent release links for Discord announcements.
Future balance notes must state the old and new values, units, exact absolute change and calculated relative percentage change. Changes to percentage-valued stats must also state percentage points.

Full notes can include mechanics, edge cases, affected modes, progression, crafting costs, world changes, interface changes, performance measurements, fixes, known issues and validation that cannot fit comfortably in a Discord announcement.
No game balance values were changed by the wiki launch. There is no verified previous-game comparison attached to this entry, so it claims no historical buffs, nerfs or percentage changes.

sections.title: Hosting and keeping pages current
items: The wiki is served from the live game’s /wiki/ subfolder. The game remains at the root URL.
The game service worker bypasses wiki requests so a cached game page cannot replace a wiki page, and wiki assets are fetched fresh.
The deployment handoff requires reviewed wiki updates and full release notes after successful live releases, then a concise Discord announcement containing the exact full-notes URL.
Secrets, hidden locations, secret rewards, triggers, discovery clues, private player data and admin tools stay out of both wiki entries and patch notes.

sections.title: Known coverage gaps
items: Public cosmetics, housing, complete mode walkthroughs, detailed controls, advanced squire care and other systems still need expanded guides.
This launch starts the detailed public release archive. Older game releases are not reconstructed from memory or presented as measured numerical comparisons.

knownIssues: Some public game systems still need fuller guide coverage; see Sources & coverage.
validation: Content checks validate quest links, prerequisites, crafting ingredients and unique entry IDs.
Browser verification covers desktop and phone layouts, search, every article, region navigation and patch-note pages.
